- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) in recent days, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise to 3% max after spike.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods — if 3 consecutive days show downward trend, add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true trend by 1–3 days — adjust by adding 0.5–1.5% to forecast if recent sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model tends to “smooth” extremes — don’t apply mean reversion unless sentiment is trending consistently.
